analysis.title: The Fed, the midterms, and what's next for the US economy
key_insights: Mizuho (Konstam, Pelle) sees the US economy closer to a cyclical upswing than a soft landing or late cycle, with persistent inflation from both supply and demand, an AI investment cycle, record corporate profits, a wealth effect and easy fiscal policy.
The war in Iran has dragged on longer than expected, keeping oil elevated and diesel near record highs.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh turned more hawkish than expected. His late-August Jackson Hole speech signaled a hawkish turn, and the Fed raised rates 25 bps in mid-September.
Mizuho expects another 50 bps of Fed hikes, with risks tilted toward front-loaded hikes.
At the September 16 press conference, Warsh said the Fed is removing 'a dose of accommodation' and that its standard for confidence that underlying inflation is moving to 2% 'has not been satisfied'.

Markets first priced hikes as reversible 'insurance'. The current path looks more likely to produce a sustained higher policy rate, and investors remain attuned to the risk of a more forceful hiking cycle.
Growth data are also strong: real GDP averaged 2.1% over the last four quarters and unemployment was 4.1% in August. Consumers, corporates and the government are spending more and saving less.
Treasury yields from 5-year notes to the 30-year bond are near multi-decade highs. Mizuho raised its end-2027 10-year yield forecast to 5% from 4.5%.
Mizuho argues the November midterms are less of a singular risk. Higher costs for goods, services and borrowing look unfavorable for incumbent Republicans.

No likely House or Senate control outcome is expected to meaningfully improve the fiscal outlook. Deficit spending stays elevated and legislative support for lower yields is unlikely near to medium term.
Mizuho sees a quick reopening of the Strait of Hormuz as increasingly challenged.
Longer term, Mizuho sees an AI-driven productivity boom that lowers inflation and lifts real growth as a scenario shaping the policies of the Fed Chair and the Trump administration.

macro_indicators.reading: +25 bps hike in mid-September (done), another +50 bps expected
macro_indicators.interpretation: Mizuho expects further hikes, with risk of front-loading, which supports higher front-end and long-end yields.

macro_indicators.reading: 2.1% average over the last four quarters
macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth is solid, supporting the cyclical upswing view and Fed hikes.
Labor market remains firm, which adds to demand-side price pressure.
Mizuho sees structurally higher yields, with current yields near multi-decade highs.

risk_factors: A more forceful or front-loaded Fed hiking cycle.
Persistent inflation from energy (diesel near record highs) and demand-side pressure.
Elevated deficit spending regardless of the midterm outcome.
Treasury yields near multi-decade highs and rising.
vol_and_positioning: Investors remain attuned to the risk of an even more forceful Fed hiking cycle, after initially pricing hikes as reversible insurance.
geopolitical: The war in Iran continues longer than anticipated, keeping oil elevated and diesel near record highs.
A quick reopening of the Strait of Hormuz looks increasingly challenged.
November US midterm elections, with incumbent Republicans disadvantaged by higher costs.
